title: Stakeholders & CSR Adventure 1: Stakeholders vs Shareholders
welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh shareholder primacy (Friedman) against stakeholder theory (Freeman).
meta_desc: Business Management: stakeholder vs shareholder approaches and stakeholder mapping.
final_note: You compared shareholder and stakeholder views of the firm and mapped stakeholders by power and interest.

concepts.def: Owner with shares; cares about returns
Any party affected by firm's actions

walkthroughs.body_html:
Two world-views of the firm.

Milton Friedman (1970): 'The social responsibility of business is to increase profits.' Maximise shareholder value within law and ethical custom.

R. Edward Freeman (1984): a firm is a network of stakeholders. Long-term value requires balancing employees, customers, suppliers, community, environment and owners.

Mendelow (1991) plots stakeholders on two axes.

Power (high/low) × Interest (high/low) gives four quadrants:

- High power, high interest: manage closely.
- High power, low interest: keep satisfied.
- Low power, high interest: keep informed.
- Low power, low interest: minimal effort.

Stakeholder conflicts: dividends vs wages, low prices vs supplier margins, expansion vs community concerns.

Reconciliation tools: profit-sharing schemes, employee share ownership, supplier partnerships, community investment, transparent reporting.
